task: Total the amount column of the attached sales CSV and print the result as TOTAL SALES.
source: Hand-made offline placeholder (no compiler or LLM call). The COBOL output is the expected output, worked out by hand; the Python output is from a real Pyodide run. npm run golden:capture replaces this file with a real capture (Req 8.1).

program.title: Total sales
lines: * Read the row count, then add up every sale
* Dress the total up for printing

steps.text: The IDENTIFICATION DIVISION names the program TOTAL-SALES. The ENVIRONMENT DIVISION stays empty: the data arrives on stdin, like a Python script reading sys.stdin.

steps.quote: Before any work, you declare every box and its exact size.
steps.text: WORKING-STORAGE declares each variable with a PIC clause. PIC S9(7)V99 is seven digits and two decimals, kept exact; Python mirrors it with Decimal. Z(6)9.99 is the printed form.
The PROCEDURE DIVISION holds the code. ACCEPT WS-COUNT reads the first stdin line, the number of rows, like int(sys.stdin.readline()) in Python.

steps.quote: We had no split(). We had UNSTRING, and we liked it.
steps.text: PERFORM VARYING loops once per row, like a Python for loop. ACCEPT reads the row and UNSTRING cuts it at the comma into region and amount, like str.split(',').
FUNCTION NUMVAL turns the amount text into a number, like Decimal(text). ADD puts it on the running total, like total += amount. END-PERFORM closes the loop.
MOVE copies the total into the edited picture, which adds the decimal point and leading spaces. DISPLAY prints it, like print(), and STOP RUN ends the program.

python.text: from decimal import Decimal, getcontext, ROUND_DOWN

narration.note: COBOL keeps money as exact fixed-point decimals (PIC S9(7)V99); Python mirrors them with Decimal, truncating to cents like COBOL.
